Get yourself an under-sink reverse osmosis filter. A decent 5 stage runs about $150, and will filter everything from fluoride to nitrates and lead.

Note that some reverse osmosis can waste as a lot of water. The very best systems can get close to a 1:1 ratio (1 gal of waste water for 1 gal of clean) however they typically have much shorter filter life and/or use integral pressure pumps (more expensive). More typically an open tank system will be closer to a 3:1 or 4:1 waste to clean water ratio. Closed tank systems (without a pump) can be as bad as 10:1 or worse. It won't bankrupt you but can be wasteful.

The waste issue isn't much of a problem if you're only using it for drinking water. If you go through a gallon a day, the waste would only add up to ~100 gal/month. If that's a problem, a little creative plumbing could use the waste to flush a toilet.
